subject.title: [Security] Permanent System Credentials Eviction Vulnerability in Redaction Registry

question: Should exact-value redaction guarantee retention for every still-active credential, and which runtime owner must deregister its raw and transformed forms when validity ends?
rationale: Current recency-based eviction conflicts with credential validity; selecting retention ownership, teardown behavior, and safe resource bounds requires explicit security-owner intent.

options.title: Owner-scoped retention
options.body: Return registration handles or scopes that pin active credential forms and remove them when the SecretRef snapshot, provider auth state, worker, or process-lifetime owner ends or rotates.

options.title: Protected permanent tier
options.body: Create a separately bounded non-evictable class for explicitly identified process-lifetime credentials while transient registrations remain evictable.

options.title: Keep best-effort semantics
options.body: Retain current eviction and explicitly accept that exact-value masking can stop before credential expiry.

recommendation.title: Owner-scoped retention
recommendation.body: Return registration handles or scopes that pin active credential forms and remove them when the SecretRef snapshot, provider auth state, worker, or process-lifetime owner ends or rotates.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged redaction/security history and co-ownership of adjacent provider credential protection make this the strongest available individual routing candidate.
